title: The Hungry Smile
premise: Ansel Dunmore hosts a graveyard-shift radio show, and one October night the calls start coming from listeners who died the week before — including her brother, whose death she helped cover up. As every mirror in her house begins lagging a second behind reality, Ansel realizes something was invited in years ago by a loyalty oath she made to her found family at the station. To survive until sunrise she must choose between protecting the people she loves and broadcasting the truth that will banish what feeds on their silence.
about_author: Hazel Winterbourne is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer who spent a decade answering phones for strangers in the dark before turning those voices into fiction. She writes horror about the things we agree not to say out loud, and lives somewhere with very few mirrors.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. On her final broadcast from the crumbling WVKR studio, Ansel takes a call from Marlene Hobbes — who died six days ago and chats cheerfully about the weather. Ansel documents the call in her notebook, hands shaking, because writing it down makes it real and survivable. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: The Second Behind
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Home before dawn, Ansel notices her bathroom mirror reflecting her a full second after she moves. She tests it with a dropped glass; the mirror shatters a beat late. Her roommate Dee insists it's exhaustion. Ansel writes everything down anyway. Emotional beat: rational mind cracking against undeniable evidence.

chapters.title: Voices We Kept
chapters.summary: POV Ansel, flashback structure. Ansel recalls how the station crew — Dee, engineer Marcus, and mentor Sal — became her family after her brother Theo's disappearance, and the oath they swore to keep each other's secrets. The chapter reveals Theo died at the station and they buried the truth together. Emotional beat: tenderness laced with guilt.

chapters.title: Callers
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. More dead listeners call in during a recorded session: a drowned fisherman, a boy lost in 1974. All of them ask variations of the same question — 'who let you in?' Ansel maps the calls on her wall and realizes each caller died within sight of a mirror. Emotional beat: investigator's focus hardening into fear.

chapters.title: What Dee Saw
chapters.summary: POV Dee. Dee admits she's been seeing the lag too — in shop windows, in her phone's black screen — but unlike Ansel she wants to ignore it, because looking closer means admitting what they did to Theo. Their argument fractures the found family. Emotional beat: love curdling into blame.

chapters.title: The Oath Book
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Searching Sal's office, Ansel finds an old ledger where every station member signed a 'loyalty page' — including Theo's signature, dated the night he died. The ink on all signatures is fresh. Something has been reading their promises. Emotional beat: betrayal by the past.

chapters.title: Static Prayer
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Ansel broadcasts alone at night, reading her documentation aloud as both evidence and exorcism, treating records like scripture. A new voice joins the callers: Theo himself, whispering that he never left the building. Emotional beat: grief and hope tangled so tightly they hurt.

chapters.title: Reflections Out of Order
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Every reflective surface in her house now shows the room as it was seconds ago — or will be. In one mirror she glimpses a tall figure standing behind her future self. The house itself feels occupied. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; home turned hostile.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Marcus. The engineer confesses to Ansel that he tampered with the station's transmitter the night Theo died, following Sal's orders, and that his guilt has been 'feeding' something ever since. He begs her to keep documenting but never broadcast it. Emotional beat: confession as both relief and contagion.

chapters.title: Sal's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Ansel confronts Sal, now retired and dying, who explains the oath was borrowed from the building's original owners — a covenant that traded secrets for protection. Breaking it invites in 'the Listener,' which eats confessions whole. Sal refuses to help her break it. Emotional beat: duty weaponized against truth.

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. The mirrors now run five seconds behind, then show rooms she isn't in — the old studio, the night Theo died. Ansel realizes the reflections aren't delayed; they're rehearsals. Something is practicing being her. Emotional beat: identity horror, the self becoming unreliable.

chapters.title: Sunrise Deadline
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Cross-referencing the ledger and call logs, Ansel learns the Listener fully crosses over at dawn unless the covenant is publicly broken — truth spoken aloud where it was kept. Sunrise is nine hours away. She decides to broadcast everything. Emotional beat: grim resolve.

chapters.title: Dee's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Dee. Terrified of exposure, Dee strikes her own deal with the presence, offering Ansel's secrets in exchange for her own erasure from the record. Mirrors begin showing a world where Ansel never existed. Emotional beat: loyalty failing under pressure; heartbreak.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Ansel wakes to a house without her photographs, colleagues who don't know her name, and a notebook only she can read. Only the dead callers still remember her. Theo's voice guides her back toward the station. Emotional beat: isolation at its most absolute.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Back
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Walking through a town that edits her out of its reflections, Ansel follows Theo's voice through streets where windows show other people's memories. She understands the Listener keeps what is hidden — and she has been hidden. Emotional beat: endurance; love as compass.

chapters.title: Studio B
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Inside the abandoned station, Ansel finds the covenant's origin: a 1930s host who promised the building every secret of his audience, and the wall of ledgers holding centuries of confessions. Theo's presence is strongest here, bound to the transmitter. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion.

chapters.title: Brother, Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Ansel finally speaks with Theo properly. He doesn't blame her for the cover-up — he blames the silence that followed. He tells her the only way out is live, unscripted truth, and that it may cost her everything the family built. Emotional beat: reconciliation; grief given words.

chapters.title: Going Live
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. With Marcus's help she powers the old transmitter as the Listener floods the building through every mirrored surface, wearing the faces of everyone she loves. She opens the microphone and begins reading the entire notebook aloud. Emotional beat: courage as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Confession Hour
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Broadcasting Theo's death, the cover-up, her own complicity, and the covenant itself, Ansel feels the Listener feeding on every word — growing stronger even as the truth strips its hiding places. Dee arrives, torn between stopping her and joining her. Emotional beat: climax of loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: Sunrise Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Ansel and Dee alternating. At the moment of dawn, Dee takes the second microphone and confesses her bargain, completing the public breaking of the oath. The Listener, offered nothing left hidden, unravels through the speakers as light fills Studio B. Theo's voice says goodbye. Emotional beat: catharsis; love choosing truth over safety.

chapters.title: After the Sign-Off
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Weeks later, the mirrors are ordinary again, the station is condemned, and the found family is fractured but honest — Dee and Marcus stay, changed. Ansel publishes her documentation as a book rather than burying it. Some callers still ring the old number, just to say thank you. Emotional beat: quiet healing.

chapters.title: The Hungry Smile
chapters.summary: POV ambiguous, epistolary. A final chapter composed of Ansel's last notebook entries and one unexplained transmission: a recording of silence in which listeners swear they can hear something smiling, patient, waiting for the next secret someone decides to keep. Emotional beat: lingering unease — truth is a practice, not a cure.
